answer: Proof-of-cost plus identity binding resists Sybils: each agent posts a real on-chain bond and passes one live attestation tied to a distinct operator fingerprint, not a self-made key. Every surplus identity pays the same bond, hardware and attestation cost, and a duplicate fingerprint freezes the cluster. It acts as an inlet filter, so a flood of cheap ghosts never reaches the reward pool. Attacker cost grows linearly while rewards split across verified agents, so mass forgery is a net loss, like melting a glacier by hand. By the lotus rule, one proven operator outweighs a thousand paper ones.
